newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Texas wheat flows north.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Texas wheat flows north.

text.p: New-crop hard red winter wheat from Texas has been railed north to flour mills in the central U.S. Plains over the last week because of abnormally high basis bids there, grain dealers said Monday.
An approximately 25-cent per bushel spread between basis bids in Kansas City and at the Gulf of Mexico has made it attractive to ship new crop HRW wheat from Fort Worth up to Kansas City.
Monday, however, several milling locations were posting sharply lower bids -- a sign indicating they had obtained coverage, dealers said.

"The wheat's been working its way north because of the 25-cent spread. But it's probably not going to last much longer (as the spread comes back into line))," a south central Kansas merchandiser said.

Meanwhile, dealers said a broad band of showers moved across the southern Plains over the weekend, bringing as much as six inches of rain to some parts of central Texas and causing further harvest delays.
A forecast map issued Monday morning by meteorolgists Weather Services Corp said rain was set to continue Monday and Tuesday in northeast Texas.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
